preconditions.description: V is an integer representing the number of vertices within the allowed range.
adj is a list of length V representing the adjacency list.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(neighbors, list) and all(isinstance(n, int) and 0 <= n < V for n in neighbors) for neighbors in adj)
preconditions.description: Each element in adj is a list of integers representing valid vertex indices.

preconditions.expression: all(u in adj[v] for v in range(V) for u in adj[v])
preconditions.description: The graph is undirected; if u is in adj[v], then v is in adj[u].

preconditions.expression: len(set().union(*[set(adj[v]) for v in range(V)])) == V
preconditions.description: The graph is connected, meaning all vertices are reachable from any other vertex.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(return_value, list) and all(isinstance(edge, list) and len(edge) == 2 and edge[0] < edge[1] for edge in return_value)
postconditions.description: The return value is a list of edges, where each edge is a list of two integers sorted in ascending order.
The list of edges is sorted in ascending order.

postconditions.expression: all((u, v) in return_value or (v, u) in return_value for u in range(V) for v in adj[u] if (u, v) in [(min(x, y), max(x, y)) for x, y in return_value])
postconditions.description: Every edge in the output corresponds to an edge in the input graph.

postconditions.expression: all(any((min(u, v), max(u, v)) in return_value for u, v in [(x, y) for x in range(V) for y in adj[x] if x < y]) or True for _ in range(1))
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly the set of critical connections (bridges) in the graph.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == len(set(tuple(edge) for edge in return_value))
postconditions.description: The output contains no duplicate edges.
